trickyParts: changie strips a YAML block body's indentation, so changeFormat indents continuation lines itself: '- {{ regexReplaceAll "\n(.)" .Body "\n  ${1}" }}' (blank lines stay empty); authors write body: as plain markdown, a |- block for several lines.
changie's error for an unknown kind does not name the file, so fold-notes renders each fragment of a failed group alone and names the ones changie refuses.

The pod's environment sets GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_*, which outrank git -c user.*: push-fold sets the four variables to github-actions[bot] for its commit; tag reads the same bot_name/bot_email constants, behaviour unchanged.
push-fold's clean-tree check ignores untracked files (the workflow downloads the notes outside the checkout anyway).
deviations: Shared push shape with INFRA-630 (agreed with its implementer over Envoy, 2026-10-27 15:40Z): land_on_main <base-sha> <workflow-file> pushes HEAD (one commit whose parent is the base) only while main's fetched tip is the base; when main moved it pushes nothing, runs 'gh workflow run <workflow-file> --ref main', and exits 0. No rebase. So push-fold builds the fold commit itself from a clean checkout of the base and lands it; there is no separate 'fold' subcommand, and the plan's refusals of a doctored commit (second commit, merge commit, paths outside the plan, a fragment edited on main since the base, a rebase conflict) have no input to act on. push-fold refuses HEAD != base, a dirty tree, and notes that are missing, extra, a symlink, empty, NUL-holding, carrying a '## ' line, or for a heading the CHANGELOG.md already has. fold_publish therefore has actions: write and GH_TOKEN in its push step.

check-release-credentials rule 7 (pin the workflow-level concurrency group) was dropped: with land_on_main two runs cannot both land a fold, so the group only saves wasted runs. The group is changelog-fold-${{ github.ref }}.

changelog-fold.yaml gained a pull_request trigger (paths: the workflow, release-push.sh, install-changie, packages/*/.changie.yaml; not .changes/**) so fold_build runs on GitHub before the merge on the PR's merge commit; fold_publish runs on main only.

Each package's fragments for one release share one notes file per (package, label); fold-plan prints tab-separated lines <package-dir> <label> <date> <path>; specs are <package-dir>[=<tag-prefix>] arguments.
Simplify pass: 5 applied, 1 skipped (git --sort=v:refname for the lowest release tag would order a tag prefix ending in digits differently from sort -V).

Round 2: push-fold defers, rather than refuses, a version-labelled group whose notes file does not exist at all (its release tag was pushed after the build planned); its fragments stay for a later run (the release's completion starts one, the daily run is the backstop). A missing main@ group's notes stay a refusal. Known limit: a new tag of a LOWER version than an existing one, pushed between the jobs on a commit holding already-planned fragments, would re-label a group and push-fold refuses (exit 1); release tags only go up.

Round 3 (review round 1): changelog-fold.yaml checks out github.sha in both jobs (no base output); fold-plan refuses every non-regular or non-.yaml entry under unreleased/ (it used to skip them silently), so the shared test fixture's README.md moved into its own refusal cases; check-release-credentials reports release-push.sh fold-notes as dependency code; land_on_main and is_commit_sha are INFRA-630's text byte for byte (architect decision, 17:29Z), land_on_main returns 0 and prints no Pushed line; check_hand_over sets no EXIT trap.

Round 4 (review round 2): fold-plan finds a fragment's first add with first_added (follows diff-tree -M renames commit by commit, never copies) instead of git log --follow, which follows copies between alike fragments and mislabels never-renamed ones (measured). Known limit: a single commit that deletes one fragment and adds a different but similar one pairs them as a rename, so the new one takes the deleted one's first add. The workflow comment and the land_on_main header paragraph corrected; no new check, per the architect.
